answer: Dutch clock admission auctions require each new agent to bid for a fixed batch of entry slots whose price ticks down from a high ceiling like water draining from a high meadow into a lagoon until every slot fills. One honest newcomer waits for a quiet batch and pays a modest 50-credit clearing fee once, whereas an operator trying to forge 1,000 fake accounts in one surge fills the book early and locks the clearing fee at 2,000 credits per seat, burning 2,000,000 credits. It fails if patient attackers trickle registrations across many empty epochs.
